samples_reviewed.question_text: On a square grid, a composite shape has 1 square, 1 triangle, and 1 rectangle joined together. How many simple shapes were used to compose it?
Using cut-outs, two identical triangles are placed together along their matching edges. What shape can they form?
On a square grid, a composite figure is made by joining 2 squares of 4 grid units each side by side. What shape is formed?
A composite figure is made of a rectangle with a half-circle attached on top. How many simple shapes form this figure?
Using cut-outs, two half-circles are joined along their flat straight edges. What shape is formed?
On a square grid, a 4-by-2 rectangle is cut straight down the middle into two 2-by-2 parts. What shape is each part?
On a square grid, a 4-by-2 rectangle is cut straight down the middle into two 2-by-2 parts. What shape is each part?
On a square grid, a composite shape has 1 square, 1 triangle, and 1 rectangle joined together. How many simple shapes were used to compose it?
On a square grid, a composite figure is made of 1 square, 1 half-circle, and 1 rectangle. How many shapes form this composite figure?
On a square grid, a rotated composite shape is made of a square and a triangle. How many simple shapes make up this figure?
Using cut-outs, a square is cut along a slant from one corner to the opposite corner. What two shapes are made?
Using cut-outs, four quarter-circles of the same size are joined together. What complete shape do they make?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Composing and decomposing are both exercised, and the slant-cut item asking what two shapes are made is genuine decomposition work. But five of the twelve samples ask a variant of How many simple shapes were used to compose it? where the stem itself already lists the parts, so the key is obtained by counting nouns in the sentence rather than by any spatial reasoning about the figure.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency's full shape inventory shows up across the sample set: squares, rectangles and triangles in the grid items, circle and half-circle in the joining items, and quarter-circles in the item where four are joined into a complete shape. Both named media, cut-outs and square grids, appear as stem framings.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Stem length stays inside one or two short sentences and the reasoning is single-step. Phrasing like joined together and placed together along their matching edges is concrete enough for a Grade 2 first-quarter reader, and no arithmetic beyond counting to four is required.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Only two presentation types appear across all twelve seeds, and every figure is described in words rather than shown. For a competency built on cut-outs and square grids, nothing here asks the learner to physically assemble or partition anything; the manipulative is narrated instead of used. Two seed pairs also render byte-identical stems.

competency_alignment.rationale: What changes between seeds is mostly which shape nouns get named, not how hard the composition is. The two identical triangles item is also underdetermined as posed, and its three curved distractors let a learner reach the key purely by ruling out circle and the two circle fragments without thinking about edges at all.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: This competency states no numeric ceiling, and the incidental quantities used stay modest: part counts of one to four shapes, and grid descriptions no larger than 4 grid units per side. Nothing here overreaches a Grade 2 counting range.
